brief: STRANGE ATTRACTORS: a 3D sculpture of chaos. Hundreds of thousands of particles (about 300k desktop, about 60k phone) flow along chaotic ODE systems, drawn with raw WebGL as additive points with depth-based size and fade, coloured by speed. At least 7 attractors with correct standard equations and parameters shown in a formula panel: Lorenz (sigma=10, rho=28, beta=8/3), Rossler (a=0.2, b=0.2, c=5.7), Aizawa, Thomas (b about 0.208186), Halvorsen (a=1.89), Dadras, Chen, Sprott. Integrate on the CPU in typed arrays with RK4 or RK2, per-attractor time steps, auto-fit scaling and centring; upload with bufferSubData each frame (or GPU integration through WebGL2 transform feedback if you make it robust). Morph smoothly when switching attractors (particles fly onto their new paths). Camera: drag to orbit, wheel/pinch to zoom, auto-rotate toggle. Controls: attractor picker, particle count, trail persistence (accumulation framebuffer with fade for motion trails), speed, palette, Scatter (re-seed particles randomly and watch the attractor capture them). Live parameter sliders for the current attractor (for example Lorenz rho from 0 to 50 to watch the onset of chaos near rho = 24.74), particle count, fps. The first frame must already show the full attractor shape (pre-integrate before the first draw).
